messages:
anita: Heads-up — saw a big latency spike in prod dedicated (us-west-2) around 07:12 UTC on the GQA/MQA mixed pool after the kernel-selector tweak we rolled yesterday. P99 for seqlen ~1024 jumped from ~120ms to ~360ms for a subset of requests. Repro traces below.

anita: Quick profiler snippet (nvprof-ish):
```
[PID 12345] kernel=fast_gqa_v2  seq=1024  tokens=768  gpu_ms=280  memcpy_ms=40  kv_page_faults=12
[PID 12346] kernel=slow_gqa_compat seq=1024 tokens=768 gpu_ms=110 memcpy_ms=12 kv_page_faults=0
```

anita: selector config we shipped: `score_thresholds: { fast_gqa_v2: 0.7, slow_gqa_compat: 0.3 }` and a seqlen_bias of `+0.5` for seq>512.

ryan: ugh. thanks for the flag. I did bump the seqlen bias to prefer fast_gqa_v2 for mid-long traces because it was winning on throughput in synthetic benches. Did we see any KV-cache churn signals?

mei: possible KV fragmentation — logs show increased `kv_page_miss` on the same hosts. When pages are more fragmented, fast_gqa_v2 ends up doing more scattered loads and memcpy. That explains memcpy_ms uptick.

josh: attaching flamegrep output from the affected host: `flamegraph.svg` (uploaded). Hot path shows `copy_kv_pages -> gather_strided` dominating.

perf-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency increased 2.9x for route `/v1/generate` on pool `gqa-mqa-mixed` between 07:10-07:20 UTC. CI microbench against fast_gqa_v2 shows degradation only when kv_frag > 8.

anita: repro script I used locally (simplified):
```bash
# simulate fragmented KV layout
python tools/sim_kv_frag.py --pages 64 --fragmentation 0.85 \
  && redwood-bench --model gqa-mqa --kernel fast_gqa_v2 --seqlen 1024 --iters 200
```
Output: p50 ~85ms, p95 ~160ms, p99 ~350ms (matches prod).

sara: can we pin the selector to prefer `slow_gqa_compat` for seq>=768 while we investigate? That should reduce tail.

ryan: agree. I'll push an override. Command: `redwoodctl routing override --pool gqa-mqa-mixed --kernel-selector \"prefer:slow_gqa_compat when seqlen>=768\" --reason \"temp rollback after 2304567 selector tweak\"`

deploy-bot: Deployment started by ryan at 07:55 UTC: override applied to pool `gqa-mqa-mixed`. Rolling config to 6 hosts.

anita: after override p99 dropped to ~140ms within 3 minutes. Good immediate mitigation. Need follow-ups:
- root cause: why does fast_gqa_v2 regression correlate with kv fragmentation?
- long-term: update kernel scoring to include kv_frag_penalty, or make kernel allocations page-aware.
- tests: add microbench perms that inject kv fragmentation in CI.

ryan: next steps: I'll open a small PR to change kernel_score from `arch_score + seqlen_bias` to `arch_score + seqlen_bias + kv_frag_penalty` and add a hysteresis window so we don't flip at small variance. Will also add a perf test with `sim_kv_frag.py`.

mei: also capturing host-level metrics (page_faults, memcpy_bytes, pcie_transfers) and tying them into kernel elect decisions would help. We should avoid hard thresholds; instead use a smoothed penalty.

josh: FYI the repro harness found that block_size=64 vs 128 changed behavior: with block_size=64 fragmentation effects amplified. Add block size sweep to the bench.

anita: great. please tag me on the PR and add a short eval that runs a few percentile checks on seqlen buckets.

ryan: will do. Opening issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-4823 — "Investigate fast_gqa_v2 regress under KV fragmentation". Assigning to `eng-runtime` and `eng-ml`.

sara: thanks all. Glad override calmed the tail. :thumbsup:
